lens: The evidence pool lacks structured, citable facts, rendering any thesis speculative; therefore, a publishable angle cannot be formed without first harvesting standardized data on exosome dosing, administration routes, and disease-specific efficacy from current literature.
known_to_ignore: Exosomes are extracellular vesicles used in intercellular communication
ISEV respondents frequently use conditioned cell culture media for EV isolation
tensions: Discrepancy in therapeutic dosing: 10 μg for intranasal instillation in bleomycin-induced lung injury vs. 30 μg for retro-orbital injection in renal injury models
Variability in diagnostic accuracy metrics for CRC exosome biomarkers (AUC 0.86-0.88) compared to lower performance for benign inflammatory disease differentiation (AUC 0.59)
gaps: Standardized dose-response relationships for exosome administration across different disease models (e.g., cancer, renal IRI, preterm birth)
Comparative analysis of EV sources (e.g., BMSCs, hAECs, HEK293) and their functional outcomes in vivo
Optimization of drug loading efficiency (e.g., DOX at 13% encapsulation) and targeted delivery mechanisms
reviewer_objections: Thesis lacks empirical support due to absence of cited evidence facts from controlled studies
Proposed angles are based on alpha hints which are untagged and not systematically reviewed, undermining scientific rigor
next_extractions: Harvest data on exosome doses (10 μg, 30 μg) and routes (intranasal, retro-orbital) from in vivo studies in disease models like lung fibrosis and renal injury
Extract specific EV sources (e.g., hAECs, BMSCs) and their mechanistic pathways (e.g., miR-146a-5p targeting IRAK1) from functional studies
Collect diagnostic performance metrics (AUC values) for exosome biomarkers in cancer staging and differentiate from benign diseases
